title: Binary Search: Interval Conventions, Boundary Updates, and Applicability
evidence_note: The supplied fixture (fixture_binary_search_en) covers closed and half-open interval conventions, midpoint computation, boundary updates, termination conditions, complexity, and applicability constraints, which is sufficient for one easy multiple-choice item.
learning_objectives: Explain what a closed search interval [left, right] represents in binary search.
State the initial values of left and right for a closed interval on an array of length n.
Identify the loop condition that matches the closed-interval convention.

sections.heading: Closed interval convention
sections.text: In binary search, a closed search interval [left, right] contains every position still eligible to hold the target. For an ascending array with distinct values and constant-time indexed access, the search starts with left = 0 and right = n - 1, and the loop runs while left <= right. An empty interval means the target is absent. The midpoint is computed as mid = left + floor((right - left) / 2).

sections.heading: Boundary updates
sections.text: After comparing the middle value with the target: equality ends the search; if the middle value is smaller than the target, all positions through mid are too small, so set left = mid + 1; if it is larger, positions from mid onward are too large, so set right = mid - 1. The interval convention determines the termination condition, and mixing conventions (for example, pairing the closed-interval test with a half-open right boundary) can inspect a position outside the array.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: Binary search depends on an ordered search space and cheap access to its middle. Sorting an unsorted array solely for one lookup adds preprocessing work, so a scan can be the better choice for that workload, while a sorted array serving many lookups can amortize preprocessing. Knowing the midpoint index does not make access to that position constant-time in a singly linked list.

expected_steps: Recall that the closed interval [left, right] remains non-empty while left <= right.
Select the matching loop condition from the options.

questions.stem: According to the supplied notes, for a closed search interval [left, right] over an ascending array with distinct values, which loop condition matches this convention?
questions.explanation: The notes state that for a closed interval [left, right], the loop runs while left <= right, and an empty interval means the target is absent. The half-open convention [left, right) instead loops while left < right.
questions.difficulty_reason: This item asks for a single explicitly stated fact from the notes: the loop condition tied to the closed-interval convention. No application, comparison, or constraint trade-off is required.
